bibliography_candidates.authors: Bobby Kleinberg, Renato Paes Leme, Jon Schneider, Yifeng Teng
bibliography_candidates.relevance: Useful analogy for the prefix-compatibility program: U-calibration is a maximal regret metric over all downstream bounded scoring rules, similar in spirit to one action sequence serving many candidate horizons or continuations.
bibliography_candidates.title: U-Calibration: Forecasting for an Unknown Agent

bibliography_candidates.relevance: Decision-theoretic calibration loss is a probability-weighted worst-case payoff-loss notion; it may supply terminology and LP analogies for replacing raw delay tails by decision-relevant information loss.
bibliography_candidates.title: Calibration Error for Decision Making

bibliography_candidates.authors: Haipeng Luo, Spandan Senapati, Vatsal Sharan
bibliography_candidates.relevance: Gives minimax results for simultaneous regret over loss families; relevant as an analogy for simultaneous-prefix and vector-deficit formulations, not as direct support for delayed market making.
bibliography_candidates.title: Optimal Multiclass U-Calibration Error and Beyond

bibliography_candidates.authors: Konstantina Bairaktari, Lunjia Hu, Huy L. Nguyen, Jonathan Ullman
bibliography_candidates.relevance: Recent actionable calibration work emphasizes measures that directly upper-bound downstream swap regret; useful terminology for an actionable delay-tail or information-loss statistic.
bibliography_candidates.title: Testable and Actionable Calibration for Full Swap Regret

ideas.risks: The cancellation can fail if the policy model leaks the evaluation horizon, if endpoint timing is misstated, or if strict-crossing limits are handled with a fixed eta that scales with N or m.
ideas.summary: Ask an explorer to turn the iteration-8 same-path multi-threshold argument into a formal finite lemma. For path old-prefix length M, then 0^N,c_1,...,c_m, verify for each horizon T_j=M+N+j that the comparator supremum using a quote approaching c_j from below is at least (N+j-1)c_j, while learner rewards from intermediate threshold-round actions before T_j are at most (j-1)c_j. This should yield R_Tj >= N c_j - sum_s A_s 1{A_s<c_j} - M.
ideas.title: Audit The No-Loss Same-Path Lift
ideas.why_promising: If correct, this promotes CL-026 in a stronger form with no O(m) finite-block loss and is the cleanest immediate extension of the accepted two-threshold anytime obstruction.

ideas.risks: The proof must track the denominator T_j=M_i+N_i+j and require m_i=o(N_i). It also must be explicit that the learner is process-aware but horizon-oblivious; a horizon-aware oracle avoids the lower bound.
ideas.summary: Use the finite same-path lemma to build one deterministic known path with blocks 0^{N_i},C_i, where C_i is the m_i-point equal-revenue threshold menu, m_i -> infinity, and M_i+m_i=o(N_i). Prove that every horizon-oblivious policy has limsup_T R_T/T >= 1/e.
ideas.title: Diagonal Same-Path 1/e Theorem
ideas.why_promising: It would give the exact same-path analogue of the accepted universal terminal-block 1/e lift and sharply separates anytime learning from horizon-aware oracle policies.

ideas.risks: A local randomized primal strategy may not compose into a global anytime upper bound. Strict crossing also requires quotes just below thresholds or a limiting argument.
ideas.summary: Solve the primal local zero-block game for finite C: minimize over action laws mu the maximum over c in C of c - E_mu[a 1{a<c}]. For equal-revenue thresholds, verify the solver's claim that the uniform law over quotes just below c_i has constant deficit r^m, matching the dual kappa(C). Then characterize the primal optimizer for arbitrary C.
ideas.title: Primal Kappa Geometry
ideas.why_promising: This would certify tightness of the finite multi-threshold lower bound and may reveal whether the block lower bounds are also local upper bounds for known-path anytime design.

ideas.risks: The condition may become tautological if defined as the final regret itself. Overlapping future maxima across blocks may prevent additive decomposition into local kappas.
ideas.summary: Formulate the process-aware horizon-oblivious deterministic-path regime as an offline simultaneous-prefix problem: choose one action sequence so that V_T^* - reward_T is small for all T. Test candidate compatibility quantities on 0^N,c_1,...,c_m blocks, sparse vanishing spikes, power-of-two spikes, and superexponential uniform spikes.
ideas.title: Known-Path Anytime Compatibility
ideas.why_promising: This is the most plausible quantifier regime for a real characterization: oracle collapse no longer applies, but raw beta failure is still not necessary.

ideas.risks: A lower-bound modulus may not imply sufficiency. Rare events, suffix compensation, and process-aware coding can make any unweighted or purely local condition misleading.
ideas.summary: Develop a probability-weighted information-loss modulus based on common-prefix events: p_u times a local kappa_I(U), minus an outside-surplus cap B_u. Compare it with U-calibration and Calibration Decision Loss as decision-relevant replacements for raw error metrics. Test it against CE-001, CE-003, CE-005, and same-path blocks.
ideas.title: Decision-Relevant Tail Modulus
ideas.why_promising: It directly targets the main obstruction in the notes: long delayed mass matters only when it is payoff-relevant, unpredictable, frequent enough, and not compensated later.

ideas.risks: The all-horizons expected-regret calculation may be delicate. If the hard branch is not revealed early enough, even a process-aware learner may suffer p_i N_i regret; if it is too revealed, the essential-sup hardness may become artificial but still useful as a stress test.
ideas.summary: Construct a rare-branch process where, with probability p_i, a code reveals entry into a long equal-revenue multi-threshold block with kappa close to 1/e, but p_i N_i is chosen to be negligible relative to relevant horizons. Compute beta, gamma, conditional kappa, Delta_T, and expected regret for law-aware policies.
ideas.title: Rare-Branch Multi-Threshold Stress Test
ideas.why_promising: This would sharpen CE-006 and show that essential-sup or conditional hardness must be probability-weighted before it can support a necessity theorem.

ideas.risks: Most arbitrary-delay results are bandit or OCO rather than public-price full-information market making. The explorer must explicitly map reward-vector observability and skipped payoff loss.
ideas.summary: Translate adaptive skipping or outstanding-observation delayed-learning algorithms to the grid market-making reduction. Aim for a bound of the form delayed-learning term plus payoff-weighted skipped-fill loss plus T/K, without knowing a tail function beta or gamma in advance.
ideas.title: Adaptive Skipping Sufficiency
ideas.why_promising: It strengthens the settled sufficiency side and aligns the theorem with modern delayed-feedback literature, where missing information and skipped observations are often more relevant than raw elapsed delay.
